# Implementation Plan: ID-scoped data.json write tooling + lazy read projections (D-001)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"overview-data-context-scalability"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/overview-data-context-scalability/plan.md`.*

## Overview

`.ralph-overview/data.json` (180 tasks, 933 KB) is the bookkeeper's single most-edited file, and edit-anchor text mutations against it are where the highest concentration of regressions happen — AGENTS.md documents **4 distinct write-safety regressions in one 2026-06-03 session**. The brainstorm (`.ralph/brainstorms/overview-data-context-scalability/selected-direction.md`, direction **D-001**) verified the seed's "every session auto-loads 173K tokens" premise is **false** (nothing `@`-autoloads data.json; the MCP server caches it in-process only), so the proven problem is **write-safety**, not read-context budget.

This plan delivers **ID-scoped write tooling + lazy read projections, additive only** — no source-storage split (no per-task files, no lifecycle buckets; those remain deferred follow-ups D-002/D-003). One shared mutation library (in the `ralph-overview` plugin) backs both a CLI surface and MCP write tools so their behavior is **bit-identical**; the watcher emits two new read-side projections; AGENTS.md is rewritten to make the helpers the canonical write path and the projections the canonical read path, demoting edit-anchor rules to a last-resort fallback; and an engine-aware PreToolUse hook (shipped in the plugin) flags raw `edit`/`apply_patch` against data.json. Two operator-in-the-loop adoption ships provide the C-6 evidence.

**This is a DUAL-REPO effort and MUST be implemented as TWO separate Ralph jobs** (see Risk Areas → "Dual-repo / two-job split"): an `ai-developer-toolkit` job (the plugin: core lib + bin subcommand + MCP tools + watcher projections + hook + release) that ships FIRST, then a `codexu` job (submodule-pointer bump + thin CLI wrapper + AGENTS.md invariants + adoption evidence) that depends on it.

## Research Findings

- Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/overview-data-context-scalability/selected-direction.md` (criteria C-1..C-8 are reproduced verbatim in Acceptance Criteria below).

### Codebase Context
- **data.json shape:** top-level `ui, generatedAt, generatedFromCommit, tasks, phaseTree, lastTouched, periodic, cadence, runs, effort, risk, workstream, sizeBucket, spawnedFrom`. Task fields: `id, scope, lifecycle, status, lastTouchedAt, kanbanCards[{className,html}], command{name,descriptionHtml,warnings,prompts{brainstorm,plan,impl}}, shipManifest{shippedAt,summary,commits[{sha,oneLine,repo?}]}`, legacy `mergeCommit`, optional `initialStage, blockedOn, members`. 180 tasks (132 merged / 36 tracked / 12 archived).
- **Byte-stability (verified):** `JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + '\n'` is **byte-identical** to the current file (933,531 bytes, **LF-only, trailing newline**). This is the canonical serialization; a no-op helper write produces a zero-byte diff.
- **Plugin read path:** `scripts/lib/parse-overview-data.mjs` exposes `parseOverviewDataJson` (plain `JSON.parse` + object-root check). `sync-core.mjs:loadOverviewData()` reads `.json` via `parseOverviewDataJson` and dispatches `.js` to the legacy AST parser. `writeSidecar()` (sync-core.mjs:521-541) → `emitDerivedArtifacts()` (emit-derived-artifacts.mjs:15-52) → `emitAgentArtifacts()` (sync-core.mjs:562-581) writes `snapshot`, `snapshotSchema`, `tasksIndex`; output paths come from `config.outputs.*` (default-config.mjs:10-22).
- **MCP server:** `tools/overview-mcp/src/server.ts:12-25` registers 6 tools via `server.registerTool(name, {description, inputSchema}, handler)`. Input schemas in `schemas.ts`; `context.ts` resolves `repoRoot`/`pluginRoot`. Package has its own `vitest` setup + `src/__tests__/`.
- **CLI boundary:** `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (codexu) is a resolver wrapper that locates the installed plugin (env → Claude cache → `~/.copilot/installed-plugins` → in-tree submodule fallback) and **spawns** the plugin's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` dispatcher. This is the precedent for a CLI surface that shares the plugin's code.
- **Atomic write:** `scripts/lib/atomic-write.mjs:atomicWriteFile()` (tmp + fsync + rename-with-retry) — reused for helper writes.
- **Hooks:** the `ralph-overview` plugin currently declares **no hooks**. Prior art for cross-engine PreToolUse hooks is `plugins/options-mode/` (Claude `hooks/hooks.json` + `hooks/pre-tool-use.js` returning `{"decision":"block","reason"}`; Copilot `.github/plugin/hooks.json` + `hooks/copilot-pre-tool-use.js` returning `{permissionDecision:"deny", permissionDecisionReason, decision:"block", reason}`).

### Technical Constraints
- **Do NOT use `loadOverviewData()` for write-side edits.** It normalizes legacy fields and could rewrite unrelated tasks. The mutation core MUST read via `parseOverviewDataJson()` (source-preserving) then validate invariants. (Protects C-7 byte-stability + minimal-diff quality.)
- **Shared-lib placement is dictated by plugin invariants #1 ("no consumer-specific defaults in production code") and #4 ("bin dispatcher is the only consumer↔plugin boundary").** The library lives IN the plugin; the consumer CLI routes through the bin dispatcher. (A lib at codexu root imported by the MCP server would break the plugin's distributability — the MCP server ships to other consumers that don't have codexu's tree.)
- **Same-plugin write contention:** every `ralph-overview` ship must bump `plugin.json` + edit plugin `AGENTS.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` + 3 marketplace indexes. Two impls touching the same plugin conflict on those files → the toolkit-side work ships as **one plugin version bump**.
- **Cross-repo two-commit rule:** toolkit changes commit inside the submodule first, then codexu records the new submodule SHA in a separate commit. A single Ralph PRD cannot span both repo roots.
- **Windows line endings:** the lib must always write **LF + trailing newline**; tests assert no CRLF is introduced (the Copilot edit-tool CRLF gotcha is sidestepped because the lib owns serialization).
- **Watcher depth-cap invariant #14:** new emitters write to `.ralph-overview/generated/` (already a watched dir at depth 0 with a basename filter for the data file) — they do not add new watch roots and must not change watch depth.

## Approach

### Architecture

**One shared mutation core, two thin surfaces, two read projections, one guard hook.**

1. **Shared mutation core (plugin-owned):** `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/lib/data-edit-core.mjs`. Pure-ish API:
   - `loadData(dataFilePath)` → `{ raw, data }` using `parseOverviewDataJson` (NOT `loadOverviewData`).
   - `applyVerb(data, verb, args)` → new `data` (deep-cloned; mutate-by-exact-id).
   - `validateInvariants(before, after, verb, targetId)` → throws on violation.
   - `serialize(data)` → `JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + '\n'` (LF).
   - `writeData(dataFilePath, serialized)` → acquire a read-mutate-write lock, `atomicWriteFile()`.
   - `unifiedDiff(beforeRaw, afterRaw)` → minimal unified diff string.
   - `runVerb({dataFile, verb, args})` → orchestrates load → apply → validate → write → returns `{ affectedId, diff }`. Both surfaces call THIS so behavior is bit-identical.
2. **CLI surface:** a `data-edit` subcommand on the plugin's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` dispatcher (`node bin/ralph-overview.mjs data-edit <verb> <task-id> [...]`). codexu adds a thin `tools/data-edit.mjs` wrapper that forwards to it (so the bookkeeper keeps `node tools/data-edit.mjs <verb>` ergonomics) + a `data-edit` package.json script.
3. **MCP surface:** 5 write tools registered in `server.ts`, each a thin handler over `runVerb`. Tool names (snake_case under `overview.` — **pending operator confirm**, default below): `overview.upsert_task`, `overview.mark_shipped`, `overview.set_lifecycle`, `overview.add_kanban_card`, `overview.set_prompts`.
4. **Read projections (watcher):** `scripts/lib/emit-projections.mjs`, called from `emitAgentArtifacts()`:
   - `active-tasks.json` — only `lifecycle === 'tracked'` tasks (today: 36).
   - `summary-projection.json` — ALL tasks, but each task's `command.prompts` and `command.descriptionHtml` replaced by the marker `{ "stripped": true, "approxBytes": <n> }` (unambiguous projection detection; chosen over `null`/omit). Drops the ~374 KB of cold prompt bodies.
   - New `config.outputs` keys `activeTasksJson` + `summaryProjectionJson` in `default-config.mjs` and codexu `.ralph-overview/config.json`.
5. **Guard hook (plugin-owned, engine-aware):** Claude `hooks/hooks.json` + `hooks/pre-tool-use-data-edit.js` (auto-discovered from `hooks/hooks.json` per invariant #5; `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is metadata-only and is NOT modified to wire the hook); Copilot `.github/plugin/hooks.json` + `hooks/copilot-pre-tool-use-data-edit.js` **AND** a `"hooks": ".github/plugin/hooks.json"` field added to `.github/plugin/plugin.json` (Copilot CLI does not auto-discover `hooks.json` — the manifest must point at it; precedent: `plugins/options-mode/.github/plugin/plugin.json` declares `"hooks": ".github/plugin/hooks.json"`). Detects an `edit`/`apply_patch`/`write` tool call whose target path matches `**/.ralph-overview/data.json` and blocks it with the engine-appropriate decision JSON, printing the `data-edit` helper invocation. (Copilot CLI does not honor `preToolUse` deny for built-in edit tools before the edit dialog renders — empirically established by options-mode v0.16.4 — so the Copilot hook is **reliable on the shell tool, best-effort on the edit tool**; the pre-commit/CI backstop is the dependable guard against external-editor edits, shell-bypassable `--deny-tool=write`, and the Copilot edit-tool gap.)

### The five verbs (mutated fields + invariants)

| Verb | Mutates | Length invariant |
|---|---|---|
| `mark-shipped <id> --summary-file <f> --commit <sha:oneLine[:repo]>...` | `lifecycle`→`merged`, `shipManifest{shippedAt,summary,commits[]}`, `lastTouchedAt` | preserved (in-place) |
| `upsert-task <id> --json <f>` | insert-or-replace whole task object | preserved if replace; **+1 if insert** |
| `set-lifecycle <id> <tracked\|merged\|archived>` | `lifecycle`, `lastTouchedAt` | preserved |
| `add-kanban-card <id> --class <c> --html <f>` | append to `kanbanCards[]` | preserved |
| `set-prompts <id> [--brainstorm <f>] [--plan <f>] [--impl <f>]` | `command.prompts.{brainstorm,plan,impl}` | preserved |

**Global invariants (every verb, enforced post-mutate, pre-write):** result re-parses as JSON; every task has a non-empty string `id`; no duplicate `id`s; `id` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+$`; target id present after write (for `upsert-task` insert, exactly one new id). On ANY violation: throw, discard tmp, leave original untouched, exit non-zero. Large values (HTML cards, multi-KB prompts, ship summaries) are passed via `--*-file <path>` or stdin to avoid shell-escaping.

### Implementation Strategy
- **Job 1 (ai-developer-toolkit, ships first):** US-T1 core lib → US-T2 bin subcommand + US-T3 MCP tools (both consume the core) → US-T4 watcher projections → US-T5 guard hook → US-T6 release ceremony. Runs as ONE plugin version bump (same-plugin contention forces serial finalization).
- **Job 2 (codexu, after Job 1 ships + pointer bump):** US-C1 submodule pointer bump → US-C2 thin CLI wrapper + config → US-C3 AGENTS.md invariants → US-C4 two adoption ships (operator-in-the-loop).

## Scope
### In Scope
- The shared mutation core + 5 verbs + invariant validation + canonical LF serialization + read-mutate-write lock + minimal unified diff.
- The `data-edit` bin subcommand + codexu thin wrapper + package.json script.
- 5 MCP write tools sharing the core + CLI↔MCP round-trip parity test.
- `active-tasks.json` + `summary-projection.json` watcher emitters (additive; `{stripped,approxBytes}` shape).
- Engine-aware PreToolUse guard hook (Claude + Copilot) shipped in the plugin.
- AGENTS.md (codexu + plugin) + README + extending docs updates.
- Helper-driven dry-run adoption evidence: fixture transcripts of `set-lifecycle` + `mark-shipped` for two distinct fixture task ids + AGENTS.md operational-practice update declaring the helper canonical for ship bookkeeping.

### Out of Scope
- Any restructuring of data.json source format (no per-task files / D-002, no lifecycle buckets / D-003, no array compaction). Source stays the monolithic JSON file.
- Replacing the watcher read path or React app data source (both still consume `snapshot.json`).
- New MCP READ tools beyond what exists.
- Prompt-trace instrumentation (the read-context measurement) — grounding already deferred it.
- **The two real-task operator-in-the-loop helper-driven ships** that exercise the helper on `.ralph-overview/data.json` directly. These depend on external task availability and operator timing, so they are deferred to a separate follow-up adoption task ("`overview-data-helper-adoption-two-real-ships`" or equivalent), filed when this Ralph job ships. The deterministic fixture/dry-run evidence in US-C4 stands in for them inside this job.

## Risk Areas
- **Dual-repo / two-job split (load-bearing).** The codexu-side stories depend on the toolkit shipping AND the submodule pointer being bumped. A single `/implement-with-ralph` PRD cannot span both repo roots, so impl MUST be two Ralph jobs (toolkit first). Do not chain the codexu job until Job 1 is on `gim-home/main` and the pointer bump lands.
- **Same-plugin serialization.** All US-T* touch one plugin and share version/AGENTS/CHANGELOG/marketplace files → run Job 1 as a single serial impl (one version bump), not parallel sub-impls.
- **`loadOverviewData` normalization trap.** Using it for writes would silently rewrite unrelated tasks → MUST use `parseOverviewDataJson`. Covered by the C-7 byte-identity test and a no-op-write test.
- **CLI requires submodule init.** The codexu `tools/data-edit.mjs` wrapper depends on `ai-developer-toolkit` being initialized (same as `bin/ralph-overview.mjs`); the error path already points at the install command. For non-codexu consumers the engine travels with the plugin (bin subcommand + MCP), so they are unaffected.
- **Windows CRLF.** Lib writes LF only; a test asserts the written bytes contain no `\r`.
- **Lost-update races.** Two near-simultaneous helper calls → wrap read-mutate-write in a lock (reuse `scripts/lib/sync-lock.mjs` pattern or a dedicated per-file lock).
- **Hook bypass.** `--deny-tool=write` is shell-bypassable and hooks miss external-editor edits → the hook targets the `edit`/`apply_patch`/`write` tool calls specifically, and a pre-commit/CI check is recommended as a backstop (documented, optional implementation). **Copilot CLI edit-tool gap:** empirically (options-mode v0.16.4) Copilot does NOT honor `preToolUse` deny for the built-in edit tool before the edit dialog renders, so the Copilot hook is reliable on the shell tool but best-effort on the edit tool; pre-commit/CI is the dependable cross-engine guard.
- **shipManifest shape drift.** `mark-shipped` must emit the existing shape `{shippedAt, summary, commits:[{sha,oneLine,repo?}]}` and set `lifecycle:"merged"` per the AGENTS.md lifecycle state machine — validated against `overview.validate_data`'s Zod schema.
- **MCP naming churn.** If the operator rejects the snake_case names, only `server.ts` + `schemas.ts` + docs change (core lib unaffected). Flagged in Open Questions.

## Acceptance Criteria
*(C-1..C-8 verbatim from the brainstorm `selected-direction.md`, with concrete verification.)*
- **C-1 helper exists and is testable.** `node tools/data-edit.mjs --help` (and `node bin/ralph-overview.mjs data-edit --help`) lists the five verbs; each verb has ≥1 passing test covering happy path + an invariant violation (e.g. `set-lifecycle nonexistent-id` exits non-zero without writing).
- **C-2 atomic-write invariants enforced.** Validates: (a) JSON parses after write, (b) `tasks.length` preserved for in-place verbs, (c) every task has a non-empty `id`, (d) no duplicate `id`s, (e) target id present after write. On any failure the temp file is discarded and `data.json` is untouched. (Test each.)
- **C-3 MCP write tools mirror CLI.** The MCP server exposes `overview.upsert_task`, `overview.mark_shipped`, `overview.set_lifecycle`, `overview.add_kanban_card`, `overview.set_prompts`; each is bit-identical to its CLI counterpart, verified by a parity test that lives in the plugin-local test suite at `tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/data-write-roundtrip.test.ts` and, for every verb, (a) seeds two byte-identical copies of a fixture `data.json` in separate tmp dirs, (b) invokes the CLI path against copy A by spawning `node bin/ralph-overview.mjs data-edit <verb> ...` as a **subprocess** (`child_process.spawnSync`) so shell/argv/exit-code/stdout-diff/write paths are exercised, (c) invokes the MCP path against copy B **in-process** through the registered MCP tool handler (the same code path `server.ts` wires) with the equivalent structured input, then (d) byte-diffs the two resulting `data.json` files (`fs.readFileSync` → `Buffer.equals`) and asserts zero-byte difference. The two surfaces MUST NOT be compared by calling the shared `runVerb`/core lib twice — the assertion is on the externally-observable write artifact reached via each surface's full invocation path.
- **C-4 watcher emits the two projections.** `active-tasks.json` contains exactly `lifecycle === 'tracked'` tasks; `summary-projection.json` contains all tasks with `command.prompts` and `command.descriptionHtml` replaced by `{stripped:true, approxBytes:N}`. Both written by the watcher in the same sync pass.
- **C-5 lint/hook fires.** All three engine-aware wirings exist and are exercised: (a) Claude PreToolUse entry in `plugins/ralph-overview/hooks/hooks.json` (auto-discovered) pointing at `hooks/pre-tool-use-data-edit.js`; (b) Copilot manifest `plugins/ralph-overview/.github/plugin/plugin.json` carries a `"hooks": ".github/plugin/hooks.json"` field (Copilot CLI requires the manifest pointer; without it the hooks file is loaded by nothing); (c) Copilot `plugins/ralph-overview/.github/plugin/hooks.json` has a `preToolUse` entry pointing at `hooks/copilot-pre-tool-use-data-edit.js`. A plugin-local unit test (e.g. `plugins/ralph-overview/hooks/__tests__/pre-tool-use-data-edit.test.mjs`) feeds a synthetic `edit` tool payload whose target path matches `**/.ralph-overview/data.json` to each hook script via `child_process.spawnSync(process.execPath, [scriptPath], { input: JSON.stringify(payload) })`, asserts the Claude script's stdout JSON contains `{"decision":"block","reason":...}` and the Copilot script's stdout JSON contains `{"permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":..., "decision":"block","reason":...}`, and asserts both `reason` strings contain the literal `data-edit` helper invocation substring (e.g. `node bin/ralph-overview.mjs data-edit`). A second payload with a non-data.json edit target asserts both scripts emit `{}` (allow). The Copilot edit-tool best-effort caveat (per US-T5) does not exempt the wiring assertions: the manifest pointer, hook entry, and synthetic-payload deny JSON must all be present and verifiable.
- **C-6 adoption evidence (deterministic, dry-run scoped).** US-C4 produces helper-driven adoption evidence that an autonomous Ralph job can verify end-to-end without depending on external task availability or operator timing: (a) a checked-in fixture copy of the current `.ralph-overview/data.json` is mutated by the helper across both load-bearing verbs (`set-lifecycle <id> merged` + `mark-shipped <id> --summary-file ... --commit ...`) for two distinct fixture task ids; (b) the captured `data-edit` invocations + their unified-diff output are recorded as test artifacts under `tests/fixtures/data-edit-adoption/` (or equivalent plugin-local path); (c) post-write `node -e "JSON.parse(...)"` of each mutated fixture exits zero and `tasks.length` is preserved; (d) AGENTS.md operational practice is updated to declare the helper canonical for ship bookkeeping and to reference these fixture transcripts as the adoption pattern. The TWO real-task operator-in-the-loop ships are deferred to a separate follow-up adoption task (see Out of Scope / Follow-ups), not gated inside this Ralph job.
- **C-7 backwards compatibility (load-bearing).** `node bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync` produces a `snapshot.json` whose `tasks` array is byte-identical to the pre-change snapshot when no source edit occurred. The new projections are additive only.
- **C-8 documentation.** AGENTS.md `## Bookkeeper operating invariants → data.json edit-anchor safety` is rewritten to declare the helpers canonical and edit-anchor rules a last-resort fallback; the ralph-overview plugin README lists the new CLI + MCP verbs.

Two Ralph jobs. Within Job 1 the clusters share one plugin's version/AGENTS/CHANGELOG/marketplace files, so finalization is serial; the cluster DAG below is for ordering, not concurrent execution. Job 2 is a separate repo and runs only after Job 1 ships + the pointer bump lands.

- Phase: 1
